claims: The study compares relation mentions in accessible OLMo/BLOOM pretraining corpora with pairwise causal judgments, and varies synthetic relation frequencies.
Reported relation frequency is positively associated with performance; reversed or negated mentions can reduce affirmative response frequency.
The context study uses GPT-4o-generated positive/negative contexts and human annotation; affirmative response rates vary substantially with context.
adverse_findings_and_limits: Affirmative response frequency is not a probability that a bank causal edge is true.
The pretraining audit is limited to accessible corpora and mostly commonsense relations; it cannot establish the behavior of every closed model.
Context can legitimately change a causal claim. Context sensitivity alone is not proof of an error; a fixed target and independently adjudicated context are required.

reread.finding: Accessible-corpus motivation and relation-prediction scope; not a universal contamination estimate.
RQ1 accessible OLMo/BLOOM corpus and synthetic-frequency interventions; RQ2 response-frequency definition; RQ3 contexts.
Context sample, thirteen annotators and Table1 affirmative ratios; contextual change can change the claim.
Conclusion and limitations: accessible corpora and predominantly commonsense relations.

supported_claims: Observed relation-frequency association and controlled synthetic exposure/context studies motivate sensitivity analysis.
The inspected source supplies no exposure upper bound for an arbitrary closed provider or this proposed banking benchmark.
Response frequency and annotator agreement do not themselves establish a causal relation as true.
